Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

# Engineering update — August

We finished the Postgres cutover on the 21st. All twelve services now read and write against the new cluster, and the old instance is in read-only standby until the 15th of next month, when we tear it down. Query latency at p95 dropped from 340ms to 190ms. Two things bit us during the move: the connection pooler defaulted to session mode, which starved the batch workers for about forty minutes, and our replication lag alert was pointed at the old host. Both are fixed.

Two people joined. Priya starts on the payments team on the 8th and will pair with Marcus for her first three weeks. Dan joins platform on the 15th. Both of them have onboarding docs assigned, and I'd ask everyone to keep the first-week questions answerable in a channel rather than a DM so the answers stay findable.

The reporting rewrite slipped. We committed to the 29th and we're now looking at the 19th of next month. The cause was the migration eating two weeks of Sam's time that we had budgeted for reporting. I underestimated that overlap when I set the date. The new date assumes no further shared load, and I've told the sales team directly.

The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

# Engineering update — September, reporting rewrite

The reporting rewrite is now targeted at the 10th of November. That is a second slip, three weeks past the 19th of October date I gave last month, and about seven weeks past the original commitment.

Last month I said the new date assumed no further shared load. That assumption held for Sam, but I made the estimate before we had opened the reporting code with the new cluster underneath it. Two things came out of that. The aggregation queries in the nightly rollup were written against the old instance's planner behaviour and three of them now take 40+ minutes instead of 4; Sam has rewritten two and the third needs the summary table we have not built yet. Separately, the finance team's two custom report definitions turned out to depend on a column we dropped in the migration, so we owe them a backfill before we can cut over.

I want to be direct about the pattern. Both slips came from me pricing the reporting work without accounting for what the migration would do to it. The 10th of November date has the rollup rewrite, the summary table, and the finance backfill each estimated separately, with a week of slack. Sales knows. If it moves again, I will bring a scope cut rather than a third date.
